sheets.summary:
What’s the deal with the Birds’ Head Haggadah? How were illuminated Haggadot from the Middle Ages created, and why does everyone make such a big fuss about them?
Dr. Marc Michael Epstein is Professor of Religion and Visual Culture and Director of Jewish Studies at Vassar College. He is the author of, among other books, The Medieval Haggadah: Art, Narrative, and Religious Imagination  and Skies of Parchment, Seas of Ink: Jewish Illuminated Manuscripts. This sheet is meant to accompany Interleaved: A Talmudic Podcast S04E06. Listen here: https://pod.fo/e/ba48e

sheets.title: Pesachim No.8: Seder Up!
sheets.summary:
Over the past tractate we’ve gotten to hear from all different kinds of experts and thinkers, and the timings couldn’t be more perfect — as we celebrate our completion of Pesachim, we are days away from practicing so much of what we have learned, with the holiday of Pesach this coming weekend. While we are delighted to share the voices from our modern day Sages with you, in every interview there is tape that doesn’t make it to the final episode cut — but that doesn’t mean there isn’t what to learn from it.  So we’ve dove back into our own audio archives to put together ideas, some we’ve shared before and some we’re excited to share for this first time here, to enhance your seder.

sheets.title: Liberation Theology - for Jews
sheets.summary: Parshat Shemot - The Exodus from Egypt is not simply an episode in the script of the Jewish People; it is the refrain. The fact that it represents the essence of the Jewish people is captured in every commandment that is זֵכֶר לִיצִיאַת מִצְרָיִם to commemorate the Exodus from Egypt.  Modern liberation movements have taken their inspiration from the exodus as a paradigm so we what does the Exodus Liberation paradigm mean for Jews and for Israel?

sheets.title: What does Sukkot Really Mean?
sheets.summary: Sukkot - Ancient holidays were repurposed by the Israelite religion to commemorate the Exodus and Sukkot appears to be the most natural. The Torah itself connects the temporary booths of the Fall harvest with the temporary boots of the migrating Israelite tribes .. or not

description.en: Passover — or Pesach, in Hebrew — is a week-long springtime festival commemorating the Exodus from Egypt. It also celebrates national redemption and freedom from slavery. It is observed through avoidance of certain foods, mainly leavened grains, and ritual dinners called Seders, where attendees retell the story of the Exodus.
description.he: חג הפסח הוא חג שנמשך שבוע וחל באביב, לזכר יציאת מצרים. הוא גם חוגג את גאולת העם והשחרור מעבדות. הוא נחגג באמצעות הימנעות ממאכלים מסוימים (במיוחד דגנים) וסעודה טקסית הנקראת ליל הסדר אשר בה מספרים המשתתפים את סיפור יציאת מצרים.

description.en: The seder is a ritual dinner and discussion held on the first or first two nights of Passover. Attendees retell the story of the exodus from Egypt and eat special foods to mark the occasion.
description.he: ליל הסדר הוא סעודה טקסית ושיחה בלילה הראשון (ובחו"ל גם השני) של חג הפסח. המשתתפים מספרים את סיפור יציאת מצרים ואוכלים מאכלים מיוחדים לציון האירוע.

description.en: The haggadah is the classic ritual text that serves as the base and script of the Passover seder. Its text was compiled during the periods of the Mishnah and the Talmud, with later medieval additions. It is the most printed Jewish book as new editions and new commentaries are published every year. Different communities around the world have also developed their own variations and ritual practices, often recorded in the editions produced in their own communities.
description.he: ההגדה היא טקסט יהודי קלאסי המהווה את הבסיס לליל הסדר. רובה של ההגדה נכתבה במהלך תקופת המשנה והתלמוד. כיום, ההגדה קיימת בנוסחים רבים בקהילות שונות אשר הוסיפו להגדה פיוטים ותפילות שונות במרוצת הדורות. ההגדה מחולקת ל-14 חלקים אשר המרכזים בהם הינם: קדש - קידוש היום, מגיד - רוב המלל שבהגדה המתאר את סיפור יציאת מצרים, מוציא מצה והלל.

en.title: The Completion of Creation
en.prompt: As the sixth day came to an end, the creation of the heavens and the earth was complete. On the seventh day, God rested, marking the end of His creative work. This day was both sanctified and blessed, signifying that the observance of Shabbat completes and sanctifies creation, highlighting the culmination of divine craftsmanship.
en.ai_prompt: The observance of Shabbat completes and sanctifies creation, marking the culmination of God's creative work. The Pesach Haggadah, the guiding text of the Passover seder, particularly the section called 'Kadesh,' introduces the concept of wholeness through the sanctification of the seventh day, Shabbat.

description.en: The Torah uses a version of the word "wholeness" in the context of a commandment to have "[completely honest](https://www.sefaria.org/Deuteronomy.25.15?lang=bi&with=Translations&lang2=en)" weights and measures and in the context of the commandment to build the altar with [whole stones](https://www.sefaria.org/Deuteronomy.27.6?lang=bi&with=Translations&lang2=en). Verses in the Prophets section of the Hebrew Bible speak of [wholeness](https://www.sefaria.org/I_Kings.8.61?lang=bi&with=Translations&lang2=en) of the [heart](https://www.sefaria.org/I_Kings.15.3?lang=bi&with=Translations&lang2=en), meaning honesty and thorough commitment. Sources of Jewish thought use the Hebrew word for "wholeness" – *sheleimut* – to talk about the goal of achieving [spiritual perfection](https://www.sefaria.org/Guide_for_the_Perplexed%2C_Part_1.2.4?lang=bi&with=all&lang2=en), discussing different types of wholeness: wholeness of intention, wholeness of heart, [physical](https://www.sefaria.org/Guide_for_the_Perplexed%2C_Part_3.28.1?ven=hebrew|Makbili_Edition,_Mif%27al_Mishneh_Torah,_2024&lang=bi) wholeness, and more.
